title: "De-bushing and soil carbon"
description: "Modelling how clearing invasive bush and pesticide use change soil carbon across Namibia, Botswana and South Africa."

Invasive bush is spreading across Southern African rangelands, choking grazing land and water. Clearing it can restore land and livelihoods, but what does it do to the carbon stored in the soil?

As a research consultant on [SteamBioAfrica](https://www.slu.se/en/research/research-catalogue/projekt/s/steambioafrica/), an EU Horizon 2020 project turning invasive woody biomass into products that benefit local communities, we modelled soil carbon dynamics after de-bushing and pesticide use in Namibia, Botswana and South Africa.

![Crop residue left on bare soil after clearing: what stays on the surface shapes how much carbon the soil keeps.](../images/residue-cover-card.jpg){fig-alt="Close-up of dark bare soil partly covered with dry straw and residue after clearing."}
